findings_addressed: FIX-3 [P2] 1/1 — NO ORACLE FOR LONGEST-PREFIX TIER MATCHING (design §5.3, the paragraph at lines 397-399 of the fix-2 doc). §5.3 freezes TierMap matching as LONGEST-PREFIX-WINS AND ORDER-INDEPENDENT, and promises in terms that reordering tiers.toml 'can never change the answer' — a property stated precisely because that file will be edited by whoever adds the next manifest. NOTHING GRADED IT. Because the frozen rule list happens to put every more-specific prefix ahead of the prefix that contains it, Slice 32 could implement FIRST-MATCH-WINS and pass the ENTIRE suite; a later edit that merely MOVED A BLOCK would then silently re-tier manifests, against an explicit promise that it cannot. CLOSED by a new AC-SBOM-23 (test_tiering.py::test_longest_prefix_wins_and_rule_order_is_irrelevant) built on an OVERLAPPING PAIR CHOSEN SO THE TWO STRATEGIES DISAGREE — 'dev/tools/' -> dev-tooling against the longer 'dev/tools/vendored-shipped/' -> shipped — since two rules that agree, or that cannot both match, make every matching strategy look identical and the criterion vacuous. FOUR ASSERTIONS: (1) LONGEST WINS — dev/tools/vendored-shipped/Cargo.toml must classify ('tier','shipped'); (2) LONGEST MATCHING, NOT LONGEST PRESENT — dev/tools/mermaid/package.json matches only the broad rule and must classify ('tier','dev-tooling'), which is what stops an implementation that answers with the longest rule IN THE MAP from passing a single-path test; (3) ORDER-INDEPENDENCE PROVED DIRECTLY — the same two rules are built into a TierMap in BOTH orders and the full verdict pair must be IDENTICAL, which an order-sensitive strategy cannot survive: it necessarily fails one of the two orderings; (4) the same paragraph's 'DUPLICATE PREFIXES ARE A LOAD-TIME ERROR' — load_tier_map() on a scratch tmp_path file carrying one prefix twice must RAISE with the prefix NAMED in the message. Neither overlapping path needs to exist on disk: classify() is a pure function of the rule set and the path string, deliberately so, since a rule for a not-yet-existing subtree must still be expressible. NO NEW CONTRACT WAS INVENTED: §5.3 already said 'load-time error', the assertion freezes no exception TYPE (none is named anywhere in the design), and the single negative constraint — that it is not UntieredManifestError — follows from that error's own stated meaning ('no rule matched THIS PATH'), since no path has been classified when a rule FILE is rejected. Design §5.3 now carries the four-row obligation table and the reasoning; §4 carries the new criterion row.

The invariant is about TierMap MATCHING ITSELF, not about the subject of any existing criterion — AC-SBOM-08 is tiers.toml COVERAGE and AC-SBOM-09 is the tier VOCABULARY — so folding it into either would have buried a promise that a whole paragraph of the spec of record turns on.
